newsitem.title: GERMANY: Former German soldiers admit attack on foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Former German soldiers admit attack on foreigners.

text.p: Five former German soldiers, on trial for grievous bodily harm and forming an armed gang, admitted on Thursday they had attacked three foreigners in March out of revenge.

The men are charged with going on the rampage wearing uniform and helmets in the western town of Detmold, threatening a teenage Italian with a knife and clubbing two Turks with baseball bats while shouting racist abuse.
The soldiers, all in their early 20s, said they had wanted revenge for an attack a week earlier by 15 young foreigners, who called them Nazis and "Army pigs".

Mirco Anders, 21, who his fellow suspects say held a knife to the throat of the Italian, said he could not remember whether he had done so. Anders and three of the other former soldiers were drunk at the time of the attack.
All the young men denied shouting right-wing slogans.

Their victims were treated in hospital for head injuries after the incident which prompted Defence Minister Volker Ruehe to order a special inquiry and hundreds of people in Detmold to take to the streets in an anti-racist demonstration.
Separate proceedings will be brought against four other former soldiers, who are also suspected of taking part in the attack, but not of inflicting bodily harm.
The army said the suspects had all just joined the army and most of them were from former communist east Germany. All nine were dismissed from the army after the incident.
